# Garmin Autoland offers added confidence to pilots and passengers in more than 2,500 aircraft


November 13, 2026


By Garmin team


### *The world’s first certified autonomous system that activates during an emergency to control and land an aircraft without human intervention is now installed on more than 2,500 aircraft and flight decks.*


Every flight comes with responsibility — and the unexpected can happen even to the most prepared pilots.[Garmin Autoland](https://www.garmin.com/en-US/autonomi/autoland/) provides an added layer of confidence by taking control in an emergency and autonomously flying and landing the aircraft if the pilot is unable to do so.1 Now equipped on more than 2,500 aircraft, this award-winning technology helps provide peace of mind to pilots and passengers alike.


## How many aircraft are using Garmin Autoland?


Garmin Autoland recently[reached a major milestone](https://www.garmin.com/en-US/newsroom/press-release/aviation/more-than-2500-aircraft-are-now-equipped-with-garmins-revolutionary-autoland-system/) , with more than 2,500 aircraft now equipped with the emergency landing system, including piston-powered aircraft and twin-engine jets.


“Surpassing 2,500 Autoland-equipped aircraft reflects the incredible adoption of a technology designed to provide pilots and passengers with added confidence when it matters most,” said Phil Straub, Garmin Executive Vice President and Managing Director, Aviation. “From the first certification in 2020 to the expansion in the general aviation market and now into twin-engine jets, Garmin Autoland continues to demonstrate certified, real-world capability across a growing range of aircraft and flight decks.”


## What is Garmin Autoland?


Garmin Autoland is the world’s first certified autonomous system that activates during an emergency to control and land an aircraft without human intervention. It is part of the Garmin Autonomí® product family, which provides active, safety-enhancing technologies that make flying easier.


## How is Garmin Autoland activated?


Garmin Autoland can automatically detect if a pilot is nonresponsive. It can also be initiated by a pilot, co-pilot or passenger. When it is activated, Garmin Autoland notifies everyone onboard the aircraft. Once engaged, no intervention is necessary for Garmin Autoland to complete an automated landing.


## How does Garmin Autoland work?


When it is activated, Garmin Autoland:


- Identifies the optimal airport for landing
- Avoids known hazards such as terrain and weather
- Announces intentions to passengers and air traffic control
- Lands the aircraft and stops the plane on the runway2


**[Read more about how Garmin Autoland provides peace of mind to pilots and passengers](https://www.garmin.com/en-ca/blog/aviation/5-ways-garmin-autoland-offers-peace-of-mind-to-aircraft-pilots-and-passengers/) .**


## What awards has Garmin Autoland received?


In 2020, the National Aeronautic Association[awarded Garmin Autoland](https://www.garmin.com/en-US/newsroom/press-release/aviation/garmin-autoland-wins-prestigious-robert-j-collier-trophy/) the prestigious Robert J. Collier Trophy. Garmin Autoland has also received a[Popular Science Best of What’s New award](https://www.garmin.com/en-US/blog/aviation/popular-science-tabs-garmin-autoland-one-of-2020s-greatest-innovations/) , a CES Innovation Award, a *FLYING Magazine* Editors’ Choice Award and Flying Innovation Award and multiple other industry honors.


## Which aircraft is Garmin Autoland certified for?


Following several years of research, development and rigorous testing, Garmin Autoland was initially certified in May 2020 on the Piper M600 SLS. Since then, it has expanded to a wide range of aircraft and can now be found on more than 15 certified models across the globe, including:


- Piper M600 SLS and M700 Fury
- Cirrus Vision Jet G2, G2+ and G3; SR20 G7+, SR22 G7+ and SR22T G7+
- Daher TBM 940, TBM 960 and TBM 980
- Select Beechcraft King Air 200, B200, 300 and 350 aircraft


The number of certified models has expanded in 2026, with Garmin Autoland certifications for HondaJet Elite II, Embraer Phenom 300EV, Pilatus PC-12 PRO and Epic E1000 AX. The HondaJet Elite II and Phenom 300EV certifications are notable for being the first of their kind among twin-engine jet aircraft.


## How is Garmin Autoland installed on aircraft?


Many of the 2,500 Autoland installations were part of Garmin integrated flight decks, including G1000® NXi, G3000® and G3000 PRIME.


[Discover the Garmin G3000 PRIME integrated flight deck](https://www.garmin.com/en-US/blog/aviation/behind-the-scenes-of-g3000-prime-how-garmin-developed-the-most-advanced-integrated-flight-deck-yet/) *.*


Nearly 250 of the 2,500 aircraft currently flying with Autoland were post-delivery retrofits, including full-retrofit King Air aircraft and eligible platforms that did not initially include the technology.


Want to learn more about Garmin Autoland? Check out our[Autoland webpage](https://www.garmin.com/en-US/autonomi/autoland/) , which includes the most up-to-date compatibility information.
